Models, enum, factories, policies, Livewire components, routes and lang keys match the contract (`app/Models/Entity.php:14-51`, `app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:64-103`, `routes/web.php:26-41`), and the required docs are updated.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes server-side (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:35,59,77`; `app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:38,50,66`), the bound entity is `#[Locked]` (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:20-21`, `app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:18-19`), action parameters are resolved and entity-checked (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:104-110`), and Blade uses `{{ }}` throughout. Minor gaps: `$targetMembershipId` is only validated manually with `filter_var` (`app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:68`), and page authorization only runs in `mount()` (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:26-31`).

tests.evidence: Pest tests cover models, policies, pick, pages, members and settings (`tests/Feature/EntityTest.php`, `tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php`, `tests/Feature/EntityPickTest.php`, `tests/Feature/EntityPagesTest.php`, `tests/Feature/EntityMembersTest.php:66-220`, `tests/Feature/EntitySettingsTest.php:23-205`), including unauthorized and tamper cases for the Members actions. Missing are unauthorized direct calls to `Settings::save`, `delete` and `transfer`, and a tamper test for `Members::$entity`.

simplicity.evidence: The change is lean and reuses the models, policies and factories rather than adding speculative abstractions. Minor duplication: `Settings::transfer()` checks the target before the transaction and then repeats the check after re-querying and locking it (`app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:74-94`), and `Members::addMember()` hand-rolls the duplicate check (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:41-45`).

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are focused and docblocks explain the intent (`app/Models/Entity.php:31-51`, `app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:104-110`). Minor issues: the transfer select reuses the `ui.role_admin` label (`resources/views/livewire/entity/settings.blade.php:25`), and the members view repeats policy checks per row (`resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:37,52`).

scope.evidence: Every added file serves the entity task: migrations, models, enum, policies, factories, Livewire pages, routes, lang files, tests and the required `docs/database-schema.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` updates. No unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features were introduced.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (add/assign/remove membership, save/delete entity, transfer ownership) are implemented directly in the Livewire components instead of one `app/Actions/*` class per use case, contrary to the project convention that domain writes live in actions and authorize inside them.

There are no unauthorized-call tests for `Settings::save`, `delete` and `transfer`; the existing 403 tests only exercise `mount()`, so the Livewire policy's requirement to test each action for an unauthorized call is not met.
The pick endpoint authorizes with a direct `membershipFor()` check instead of the existing `EntityPolicy::view` gate, splitting authorization between the controller and the policy layer.

The "never remove the last manager" rule is authorization logic in the component rather than in `EntityMembershipPolicy::delete` (or an action), so future callers of the policy would not get this invariant.

`$targetMembershipId` is a public client-writable property with no `#[Validate]`/`rules()` declaration and is only checked manually with `filter_var`, contrary to Livewire policy rule 1; add a declarative integer rule and call `$this->validate()`.

Page authorization runs only in `mount()`, so a user removed from or demoted in the entity while a page is open can still trigger a Livewire refresh and read the page's rendered data because `render()` does not re-authorize; re-check the policy in `render()` or in a persistent guard.

The "owner row disappeared" test deletes the owner before calling `transfer()`, so the `manageSettings` check at the start of `transfer()` fails first; the in-transaction owner-null branch is never exercised and the test passes for the wrong reason.

`transfer()` validates the target before the transaction and then repeats the same check after re-querying and locking the target; the pre-check is redundant and can drift from the authoritative check.

Each member row calls `@can('assignRole')` and `@can('delete')`, and each policy call runs `membershipFor()`, producing an N+1 query pattern on the members page; compute the current user's role once and pass booleans or flags to the view.
The transfer select is labelled with `ui.role_admin` ("Admin"), which describes the option's current role rather than the field's purpose; a dedicated "new owner" label would be clearer.

The duplicate-membership check is hand-rolled with a query plus `ValidationException`; a `Rule::unique('entity_memberships')->where(...)` rule (or relying on the named unique index) would be less code and consistent with the slug validation.

The last-manager guard also blocks an employee from removing themselves when the entity currently has no owner/admin rows, although the task only forbids removing the last manager; consider applying the guard only when the target is a manager.

review.summary: The change implements the entity data model, policies, pick endpoint and Livewire dashboard/members/settings pages, and it is largely functionally complete with broad test coverage. It nevertheless needs changes before merging because it bypasses the required `app/Actions` layer for domain writes and omits unauthorized-call tests for the Settings actions; the remaining findings are minor policy, validation, test and N+1 concerns.
